Philosophy, decisions & perspective

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Readable introductions and small models for examining an idea, comparing interpretations, and thinking through a choice.

A clear explanation can help you notice an assumption you had not considered. Philosophy offers arguments to examine, while a model makes selected relationships easier to see. Neither requires treating life as a puzzle with one hidden correct answer.

Start with: A first encounter with philosophy. Open the Introduction or Approaching philosophy section. The full course is optional.

A first encounter with philosophy

The Open University, OpenLearn

An invitation to examine arguments rather than collect impressive names. You can sample the activity of philosophy without adopting a complete system.

Begin here: Open the Introduction or Approaching philosophy section. The full course is optional.

Access: Free course text can be started without registration; progress, quizzes, and participation features use an account.

Poetry Unbound: one poem at a time

The On Being Project; hosted by Pádraig Ó Tuama

A different kind of attention, with no task to optimize. This selection leaves room for an unexpected moment to matter without pretending it fixes everything.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Begin with an introductory passage or one interactive example. Ask what the argument assumes, what the model leaves out, and whether its conclusions fit the question you actually have. A useful analogy can illuminate a decision without reducing relationships or personal values to a numerical score.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
